page: Microsoft Azure E16bds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine configuration built within the Ebdsv6 series on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel processor providing 16 dedicated virtual CPUs. The host configuration pairs these cores with 128 GB of system RAM, delivering an 8 GB per vCPU ratio suitable for applications constrained by physical memory capacity. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs included on the platform.

Storage architecture incorporates a bundled 945 GB local NVMe solid-state drive designated for high-speed scratchpad use, temporary files, and low-latency buffer storage. The instance family features enhanced remote block storage performance and supports Azure Premium Storage for persistent managed disks requiring predictable input-output operations. Network configurations do not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating routing through private network constructs or provisioned public IP resources.

The architectural balance of the E16bds_v6 emphasizes high memory density and block storage capabilities over raw compute density. The inclusion of dedicated vCPUs guarantees consistent compute baseline allocation without hypervisor-level CPU contention. Qualitative cost efficiency stems from consolidating large memory and local NVMe requirements into a single multi-core instance, which reduces the need to scale to higher core-count VMs solely for memory expansion. Primary workload fits include enterprise relational database management systems, in-memory caches, ETL batch transformations, and data analysis pipelines requiring large working memory sets and local swap storage.
description: Microsoft Azure E16bds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Ebdsv6 family, designed for high memory requirements and elevated remote block storage throughput. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance supplies 16 dedicated x86_64 virtual processing units backed by an Intel processor, alongside 128 GB of system RAM, maintaining an 8 GB per vCPU allocation ratio. Local storage consists of a bundled 945 GB NVMe SSD, suitable for scratch space, temporary indexing, or cache directories, while external disks can utilize Azure Premium Storage. The server provides no hardware GPU acceleration or complimentary public IPv4 addressing. The balance between dedicated compute allocation, an elevated memory footprint, and high-speed local disk capacity positions the instance for memory-heavy transactional databases, in-memory caching systems, distributed data processing nodes, and intermediate analytics pipelines where RAM volume and low-latency ephemeral input-output operations are primary architectural requirements.
